description: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library building. This beautifully preserved Edwardian building is rich in architectural character and heritage, featuring stunning stained glass windows, an impressive dome, ornate door handles, and a historic brass plaque. Discover the history and craftsmanship of this remarkable community landmark during your visit.

factsheet.heading: Visit the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library
paragraphs:
Visit our beautiful Grade II listed Edwardian Corbett Community Library. Opened on 3 November 1907 with funding from Scottish philanthropist Andrew Carnegie, the library has been sympathetically refurbished while retaining original features, including its impressive glass dome, stained glass windows and ornate door handles.
If a volunteer is available during your visit, we will be delighted to offer an informal tour of the building, providing additional insights into its history and unique features. We are also happy to share the story of the library's transformation from a council-run service to a thriving community library powered by volunteers, as we look ahead to celebrating our 10th anniversary in October.
